newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ non-residential building consents up in Dec-SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ non-residential building consents up in Dec-SNZ.

text.p: The value of consents for non-residential buildings increased again for the December month, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
Consents with a total value of NZ$2.567 billion were authorised for non-residential buildings in the year ended December 1996, an increase of 25.8 percent from the year ended December 1995.
The value of non-residential consents for the month of December 1996 was $246 million.

SNZ said this figure included: $51.5 million for education buildings; $47.9 million for factories and industrial buildings; $38.4 million for social, cultural, religious and recreational buildings; $27.5 million for offices and administration buildings; and $25.3 million for storage buildings.

The value of consents for residential buildings (new dwellings and outbuildings plus alterations and additions) in December 1996 was $287.9 million, an increase of 11.0 percent from December 1995. Consents for 1,803 new dwelling units were issued in December 1996.
"The national median consent value for new dwelling units authorised in December 1996 was $188,300, a decrease of 1.4 percent when compared with the December 1995 figure," SNZ said.
It said the total value of consents for the year ended December 1996 for all buildings was $6.219 billion, an increase of 17.1 percent from the $5.312 billion issued in the year ended December 1995.
